A non-degraded Ok verdict implies the authoritative admission state was reachable, that
state is ABOUT the workload the call is bound to — its `admission_id` equals the
authenticated admission's, which `authenticate_admission` has already equated with the
call's binding and with the verified assertion's — and at that workload its generation
equals the authenticated generation (the binding's) and its status is Admitted.

The three conjuncts are ordered, and the order is the claim. Generation equality and
`Admitted` are properties OF a subject; asserted about an unnamed record they are satisfied
by any workload that happens to sit at the same number, and a generation is a per-workload
counter, so that is the ordinary case rather than a contrived one.

corrections.new:
Over the MATERIALIZED identities, and that is the substance of the claim rather than an
implementation note. A comparison of mechanism LOCATORS would establish nothing: an ARN, a key
id and an alias are three names for one AWS key, a PKCS#11 label is scoped to a token, and a
filesystem path resolves through symlinks — two locators that differ can be one key, and a
check comparing them would report a separation that does not exist while looking exactly like
one that does. So both roles are asked for their public verification key after materialization
and compared as `Ed25519PublicKeyValue`, the canonical RFC 8410 identity this crate already
owns. No AWS-, GCP- or PKCS#11-specific equality semantics were invented.

UNCONDITIONAL, and deliberately not conditioned on a policy input. The ratified wording is
"where policy requires the roles to be distinct"; measurement found no supported deployment
for which sharing is desirable, and inventing a one-valued policy knob to make the condition
expressible would fabricate an input that selects nothing. Every deployment is held to it, so
the conditional is satisfied everywhere rather than left as a dormant branch.

It is load-bearing rather than a construction-site convention, which is what moved it here.
`MaterializedSigningRoles` holds the source privately and `establish` is its only producer, so
a serving path cannot hold a key source that did not come through the comparison — deleting
the call does not leave a path that skips it, it leaves one that does not compile. What that
does NOT settle is whether the composition root uses the materializer at all: `FileKeySource`
and the KMS adapters are public constructors that external embedders need, and THM-0082 is
what measures the root.

The owner moved from `proxy.cross_machine_legality`, and had to: a request-level classifier
reads locators, and the decisive fact here exists only once both backends have answered. X2a
(THM-0049) states the adjacent relation — that the channel key object lives in a backend the
deployment already reaches — and is not this claim.

A channel credential whose public key is not a canonical Ed25519 key yields no comparison, and
that is a statement rather than a gap: the response role's key always is one, so the two cannot
be equal. Likewise a role that materialized NO key contributes none — the composition root
reads both immediately afterwards to build the listener and the delegation, so a deployment
where either is unavailable starts no server, and the only executions that arm admits are
executions that never serve.

That reading is measured and not merely argued. `proxy.signing_credential_provenance`, the unit
that carries THM-0082, pins both reads: `the_composition_root_reads_both_signing_roles_eagerly_and_fallibly`
goes red when the channel chain or the response key is read lazily or has its failure swallowed,
and `M432` is the probe that swallows it. This claim therefore rests on that control for the one
clause the materializer cannot seal.

TWO PREMISES, both found by the missing-edge pass over this very claim rather than assumed.
The comparison is over `raw_point()`, so "different points implies different keys" needs
THM-0025: possession of an `Ed25519PublicKeyValue` means it was interpreted from the canonical
RFC 8410 encoding and its projected point IS those bytes. Without that the inequality would be
about two projections rather than about two keys. And the claim that the LEAF's key is the
CHANNEL-SIGNING key is not free either — on the delegated path it is THM-0027, which
establishes that a resolver cannot exist over a credential and a signer that do not correspond,
which is what makes the served leaf the key that signs the handshake.

It claims nothing about whether either key is the RIGHT one, about custody, about exposure, or
about the chain being trusted.

corrections.new:
A second verified actor who knows the open leg's public evidence handles cannot obtain
the victim's retained handles, so it cannot complete a human-approval round trip that was not
its own. A refused or transiently-failed read cannot destroy a live approval either.

The consequence is about an actor reaching the store THROUGH this proxy. One that can write
the keyspace directly needs no victim's handles — it plants its own — and that is ASM-0047's,
not this claim's.

the victim's retained bases, so it cannot complete a human-approval round trip that was not
its own. A refused or transiently-failed read cannot destroy a live approval either.

corrections.new:
RUNTIME CORRELATION AND REACHABILITY ONLY. It is about which actor can reach a live
continuation entry and about the entry surviving a read that admits nothing — not about
deployment posture, and not about whether the shared tier this deployment holds is the one its
configuration selected. That materialization claim is THM-0077's and is not restated here.

NO "PREVENTS STARTUP" CONJUNCT APPEARS, because startup posture is a different authority's
fact and not because this claim is indifferent to it. Which capability the runtime installs
for the plan it was given — including that a SELECTED store this build cannot provide, or
cannot establish, refuses startup by name rather than being announced as OFF — is THM-0096's
and is deliberately not restated here. What an answer leg may proceed on, and how a
request-time absence is attributed between the caller and the deployment, is THM-0093's.
This claim observes its own `ContinuationPlane` state and consumes no proposition from
either.

That paragraph previously read "the store is OPPORTUNISTIC ... an unavailable shared tier
does not refuse startup — the deployment announces its absence and serves — and an answer
leg that needs a correlated continuation fails closed at the binding". Both halves described
behaviour the tree no longer has: the capability has a dedicated selector
(`--continuation-control-redis-url`), a selected capability is never silently downgraded,
and a deployment-side absence is refused before admission as a fact about the DEPLOYMENT
rather than at the binding as a fact about the caller. The claim itself did not move — it is
about keying and the non-consuming read — so what is corrected is the reason given for a
boundary that was always correctly drawn.

THE PROVENANCE IS COMPOSED, NOT LOCAL, and the composition is named because the alternative is
to imply a stronger local fact than exists. THM-0051 establishes that the product the serving
path carries is the one THIS exchange's verification returned, and THM-0014 — inside THM-0051's
own closure — that the actor in it was resolved through the trust seam. What
`unit://proxy.continuation_key_provenance` measures is the remaining step: that both legs
supply that product's actor projection to the key and nothing else, defended by probe M88.

No type makes this true by construction, and none is claimed to. `ResolvedActor` is
deliberately unsealed and legitimately constructible through the resolver seam, so a projection
of one establishes only what it was handed; the provenance is earned by the chain above and by
the controls, never by a constructor's argument type.

WHAT THE KEY'S DIGEST CONTRIBUTES, AND WHAT IT ASSUMES. The derivation is injective over the
(audience, resolved actor, state) triple as an ENCODING; that two distinct triples do not
address one entry is a statement about the DIGEST, and rests on SHA-256 second-preimage
resistance, registered for this unit alone as ASM-0060. It is deliberately not ASM-0028's
(whose scope is the six digest-equals-bytes propositions) and not collision resistance.

WHAT "REACHABLE" QUANTIFIES OVER: requests that reach this proxy. Every path by which an
entry is read or removed through MCP-RE derives its key from the resolved actor, and that is
the whole of what is measured. A party with direct WRITE access to the `mcp-re:cont:`
keyspace falls outside the quantifier — it does not reach the victim's entry, it creates its
own under a key derived from its own actor, and the answer leg's digest equality then holds
against bytes this fleet never produced. That premise is ASM-0047, registered rather than
argued, because the reading the title would otherwise invite — that the entry is unreachable
full stop — is one no deployment can support. ASM-0048 carries the rest of what the store
contributes: the `DEL` count that makes removal one-shot across replicas, and the `PX` expiry
that bounds an unanswered approval's life.

It says nothing about what an acknowledged write durably establishes, and nothing about the
continuation binding itself, which is `mcp-re-http-profile`'s.

corrections.new:
REFUSED AT CONNECT, NOT TRUSTED AT RUNTIME. The store asks the server for its
`maxmemory-policy` and refuses to open at all unless the answer is `noeviction`. Every
`volatile-*` and `allkeys-*` policy is refused by name, case-insensitively because the reply
is a server string rather than a token this code chose. **A policy it could not read is
refused too**: an empty reply, an error, a renamed `CONFIG` — an unverifiable policy is not
evidence of a safe one.

THE WINDOW IS A WINDOW. The `PX` TTL is the retention horizon plus the declared replica clock divergence
bound, minus `now` read from the store's OWN clock, never an absolute epoch, and it clamps to a
minimal value rather than going negative when the instant has already passed. The padding is what
makes the window safe for a replica whose clock runs ahead of a correct one: the record is kept to
the verifier's horizon in true time for every clock within the declared bound, and that the actual
divergence is within the bound is ASM-0061. An already-stale `retain_until` is refused BEFORE Redis
is touched, judged on the unpadded horizon.

THE DECLARED TIER IS ENFORCED, NOT AUDITED. Where `REDIS_WAIT_QUORUM` is selected, a fresh
insert is followed by `WAIT`, and an acknowledgement shortfall FAILS CLOSED — it does not
report the nonce fresh and note the shortfall.

EVERY NON-ANSWER IS AN OUTAGE. A stall is bounded by a timeout rather than hanging; a refused
endpoint fails closed at construction rather than after the deadline; a transient error is
retried only where retry is safe and a fatal one is not retried at all; a reconnect that
itself fails, fails closed. Connect attempts that were abandoned are bounded by a ceiling
which also fails closed, and one stalled connect strands at most one permit. No path returns
`Fresh`.

corrections.new:
NOTHING ABOUT DURABILITY. What an acknowledged `SET NX` durably established is ASM-0040, a
foreign premise with its documented failover caveat — `REDIS_WAIT_QUORUM` is not linearizable
replay durability and is not a guarantee that every later failover preserves the nonce.
Nothing here restates it or strengthens it, and this theorem is not evidence for it.

NOT A LIVENESS CLAIM: it says no failure becomes a `Fresh`, never that a healthy Redis
answers.

THE POLICY IS ASSERTED AT CONNECT, ON EVERY CONNECTION, AND NOT AFTERWARDS. Each pooled
connection asks the server it reached, so a URL that resolves to a different server per
connection is refused if any of them evicts. A server whose policy is changed underneath a
live connection, or a failover or reconnect that lands a live connection on a different
server, is not detected by this mechanism, and nothing here claims otherwise. What covers
that is ASM-0059 — every server reachable at the replay URL, failover targets and
replacements included, runs `noeviction` for as long as it serves the tier — an operator
premise this claim rests on rather than establishes. The connect-time refusal is what stops a
misconfigured deployment from starting rather than what stops one from being reconfigured.

The `WAIT` conjunct governs the tier the store was BUILT with. That the tier a deployment
DECLARED is the tier the store was built with is `app.rs`'s composition and THM-0092's
subject, not this one's.

Measured in the `redis_replay` feature lane named by the owning unit — the crate's
default-feature test targets compile these files to zero tests. Executable, class V0.

corrections.new:
ONE LINEARIZED ADMISSION. The record is a `v3/kv/txn` comparing `CREATE_REVISION == 0` and
PUTting the key under a lease iff it does not yet exist. Etcd linearizes the transaction, so
two racing inserts cannot both observe the key absent: `succeeded` is `Fresh`, and
not-`succeeded` is `Replay`.

THE LEASE IS BOUNDED, AND IS A WINDOW. The lease TTL is the retention horizon plus the declared
replica clock divergence bound, minus `now` on the store's OWN clock, clamped to a minimal value
rather than going negative, so a replica whose clock runs ahead of a correct one still keeps the
record to the verifier's horizon in true time (the bound being true is ASM-0061). A recorded nonce
self-expires at that padded horizon even if the proxy dies. An already-stale `retain_until`
is refused with NO etcd call at all. Nonces retained to the same instant share one lease, so
the outstanding-lease count grows with the freshness window rather than with request volume,
and an expired lease is never reused.

THE LEASE A REPLAY DID NOT USE IS GIVEN BACK. A `Replay` revokes the lease it minted and did
not consume; a `Fresh` keeps it. A revoke that FAILS still answers `Replay` and never an
error — the nonce's status is already known, and turning lease hygiene into a refusal would
convert a bookkeeping failure into a denial of service.

FAIL CLOSED, AND BOUNDED. A lease id that is missing, zero or unparseable is refused. Every
transport, status, parse or TIMEOUT outcome is `Unavailable`. The per-operation deadline is
clamped at BOTH ends and applies to every one of the three POSTs, because an awaited future
that never completes holds its request and its admission slot forever — a black-holed
endpoint would otherwise consume the whole `--max-in-flight` budget without a single invalid
request being sent.
